thread:
morgan: Quick question — I'm trying to pull the raw log lines for a request that only shows up in the trace. Header we set is `X-Request-Ref: 8a3b9f` and trace id is `ab12cdef3456`. Console trace view shows the proxy span but I can't find the exact log line in logging console. Anyone know the shortest path to grab raw lines?

alex: If you have the trace id, start by opening the tracing UI and click the proxy span to get the raw span tags. It usually includes request headers or the upstream id. But for raw logs I usually go to the node that served the request and grep.

jen: Agree with Alex. If you want a quick CLI path (no console), try stern targeting the proxy pod and filter by the request-ref header. Example I use:```bash
stern -n prod 'edge-proxy' --since 10m | rg "X-Request-Ref: 8a3b9f"```

morgan: I tried stern but the cluster is noisy and I might have missed the time window. Is there a way to search logs centrally with trace id?

alex: Yes — rlog has a trace->logs mode. Something like:```bash
rlog find --trace ab12cdef3456 --env prod --format raw```That will try to pull recorded log lines that have span/trace linkage.

jen: If rlog returns nothing, check whether the proxy is injecting the trace id into logs. Some older builds only write trace id in span attributes, not in log lines. You can cross-check the proxy pod's log config: /etc/logging/format or look at the configmap `proxy-logging` in prod.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed: proxy v2.11 rolled at 2026-02-18; that version toggles structured logging. If the request hit a canary node on v2.10 it may be missing header fields in raw lines.

morgan: Good catch. How do I map the trace -> pod if the trace only has container id? Console shows a span attribute `k8s.pod: proxy-5b7d9`.

alex: Use kubectl to query that pod for logs with timestamps around the span start. e.g.:```bash
kubectl -n prod logs proxy-5b7d9 -c proxy --since=30m | rg "8a3b9f|ab12cdef"```If the pod rotated logs, you might need to check previous logs or the node logging store.

jen: Another trick: the trace UI has a link to the host and container id in the span details. Click that -> it includes a direct link to the logs view in Console (Observability -> Logs -> query with pod name prefilled). That often narrows it down faster than grepping the whole cluster.

morgan: That console link is gold — hadn't noticed the pod->logs jump. One more: if logs are ingested with JSON keys, what's the best grep? I tried rg against `X-Request-Ref` but the ingester renames keys to `req_ref` sometimes.

alex: For JSON logs use jq-ish matcher in rlog or use `rg '"req_ref"\s*:\s*"8a3b9f"'`. Or in Console use `json.payload.req_ref:"8a3b9f"` (Console query language).

jen: If nothing shows up and rlog trace->logs returns empty, open a ticket in #eng-sre and paste the trace id + earliest timestamp; SRE can check raw node files and archiving.

morgan: Thanks all — steps I will try: 1) open span and use pod link, 2) rlog find --trace, 3) stern on specific pod, 4) escalate if archived. Will post results here. :thumbsup:
